To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the nuclear symmetry energy is extremely uncertain at suprasatuation densities, and that the in-medium three-nucleon interaction is a major uncertainty in the symmetry energy at high densities.

(i) the in-medium three-nucleon interaction and the short-range two-nucleon tensor force owing to rho meson exchange both contribute to the high-density behavior (especially at suprasatuation density and beyond) of the symmetry energy; (ii) the three-nucleon force and the rho meson tensor force are of comparable strength in determining the high-density behavior; (iii) the short-range nucleonic correlations are also important in determining the high density behavior of the symmetry energy

the nuclear symmetry energy can be very large at densities beyond the saturation density, and its high-density behavior can be strongly influenced by the three-body force and the short-range nuclear correlation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a better understanding of the nuclear symmetry energies at high densities.

a systematic study of effects of the nuclear three-body interaction and of the rho meson short-range correlation on the high density behavior of the nuclear incompressibility, symmetry energy, and the slope of symmetry energy.
the high-density behavior and uncertainties of the nuclear symmetry energies in the framework of the interacting Fermi-gas model.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the uncertainty in the high-density behavior is still large and the nuclear symmetry energy may be as low as 10-20 MeV at 3-4 times the normal density, which is much lower than the value obtained by using the Skyrme-type effective interactions.

the uncertainty of the nuclear symmetry at densities beyond the nuclear saturation density is still large, which is not surprising in view of the complexity of the underlying physics and the difficulty of the relevant experiments, especially for the high-density behavior.
the high-density behavior (especially the curvature of the symmetry energy) is not yet well established.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the in-medium three-nucleon force and the short-range correlation are the two most important sources of uncertainty in the nuclear symmetry energies at high densities, which should be taken seriously in the future studies of the high-density nuclear matter.
, in addition to the in-medium three-nucleon interaction, the two-body short range tensor force is also an important ingredient to the nuclear symmetry energy.
the nuclear symmetry energy has a very large uncertainty at suprasatuation densities and it can only be determined by future experiments.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the uncertainty of the high-density behavior in the nuclear symmetry is mainly due to the poorly known in-medium three-body nuclear force.
the uncertainty of the nuclear symmetry pressure at suprasatuation densities is mainly from the in-medium three-nucleon force and the short-range nucleons correlation.

the uncertainty of the nuclear symmetry energies at suprasatuation densities is not a simple matter of the model-dependence, but rather is a result of the interplay of the many-body effects in the nuclear medium.
